thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall (level: page) for incidents@redwood — latency SLO breach detected on hosted redwood-13b-quant in shared-gpu-pool-3, p99 > 1s for the last 5m. @Maya, @Jordan are on the rotation.

Maya: I’m up. seeing alerts too — p95 jumped to ~420ms, p99 at ~1.15s, streaming stalls increasing. digging into pool metrics now.

Jordan: on my way. which tenants are the top offenders?

Maya: quick top-3 by QPS: tenant-acme (~32% of tokens), tenant-lumos (~18%), tenant-rocket (~12%). acme is the one spiking writes/IO according to metrics.

Samir: tagging infra — this looks like noisy-io not raw GPU compute. kernel writeback and blkio saturated on nodes gpu-3a/3b. I can pull iostat.

Maya: dropping a short metric snapshot:
```
Metric snapshot (5m window):
- pool: shared-gpu-pool-3
- requests: 1200 rps
- p95 latency: 420 ms
- p99 latency: 1150 ms
- streaming stall count: 86 -> baseline 10
- blkio util (avg): 92%
- write_kb/s (gpu-3a): 320MB/s
```

Jordan: thanks. link to perf dashboard: https://console.redwood/prod/dashboards/pool/shared-gpu-pool-3?range=5m

Caroline: customer-impact note: acme is on a high-volume inference campaign — they reported intermittent slowdowns in the last 15m via support. we should prepare a brief for support.

Samir: iostat from gpu-3a (last 30s):
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s   rMB/s  wMB/s await  %util
nvme0n1          1.2    420   0.02   300   18.2  95.7
nvme1n1          0.4    10    0.00   2     2.1   8.0
```
blkio shows throttling messages in dmesg for cgroup blkio throttle.

Maya: confirms cgroup io throttle triggering. likely tenant-acme has a write-heavy workload (embedding/cache writes) stomping shared NVMe.

Jordan: mitigation idea A: quick-evac of tenant-acme to a dedicated pool with higher IO QoS. Mitigation B: bump blkio throttle for acme (risk: impacts others). Which is faster?

Samir: bumping blkio limits requires editing cgroup config + rolling restart of the tenant pod — low risk but may take ~3-4 minutes. Evac to dedicated pool via scheduler `reassign-tenant` should be ~1-2 min if capacity free.

Maya: capacity check — dedicated-io-1 has 20% headroom right now. I can migrate one host there.

Jordan: do the migration. runbook command: `redwoodctl tenant migrate --tenant tenant-acme --from shared-gpu-pool-3 --to dedicated-io-1 --mode live`

Maya: running migration now. pasting command and PID.
```
$ redwoodctl tenant migrate --tenant tenant-acme --from shared-gpu-pool-3 --to dedicated-io-1 --mode live
Migration started (id=mig-20250308-01)
Steps: checkpoint -> reassign -> warmup -> cutover
```

ops-bot: Migration job mig-20250308-01 moved 3 pods, checkpoint OK, warming up 2 new replicas.

Samir: watching node metrics. NVMe write_kb/s on gpu-3a dropped from 320MB/s -> 85MB/s within 40s of pods being moved. blkio throttle count decreased.

Maya: visible improvement in latencies: p95 -> 210ms, p99 -> 430ms, streaming stalls down to 12.

Caroline: preparing customer update: "We mitigated transient latency by moving high-throughput jobs to isolated capacity; monitoring closely; no data loss expected." Adding ETA for full stabilization ~10-15m.

Jordan: great. leaving a note: created a follow-up EPIC to add per-tenant disk I/O accounting and auto-evac rule.

Samir: follow-up log excerpts for postmortem:
```
Mar 08 12:34:10 gpu-3a kernel: blkio: cgroup blkio throttling in effect, id=542
Mar 08 12:34:30 scheduler: tenant-acme write_kb/s=320384
Mar 08 12:35:10 scheduler: tenant-acme qps=18.4 p99=1.12s
```

Maya: creating incident ticket INC-20250308-77 with summary + initial severity = Sev3. tagging oncall, infra, eng-runtime, cs.

Jordan: handoff: I need to step out in 10m. @Ryan can you take incident lead for the next 2 hours? quick summary: noisy-io from tenant-acme caused blkio throttles in shared-gpu-pool-3, migration to dedicated pool mitigated latencies. monitor for >30m before closure.

Ryan: taking lead. will keep watch. adding runbook tasks to the ticket: 1) verify 30m stabilization window, 2) run tenant IO profile, 3) schedule follow-up retro.

Caroline: customer comms sent to support in staging: "We identified and mitigated the issue; we are monitoring and will follow up with timeline and root cause in 24h."

Samir: quick checklist for retro: - capture per-node blkio events - correlate tenant write patterns - verify eviction/migration telemetry - propose autoscale/evac trigger threshold (e.g., write_kb/s > 200MB/s sustained for 60s).

Maya: adding note re: streaming stalls: codepath uses disk-backed KV cache for long contexts — we should consider increasing in-memory cache for hot tenants.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20250308-77 updated: status -> monitoring, assigned -> Ryan, priority -> P2.

Ryan: I'll leave the monitoring and will update the ticket in 30m. root cause candidate: tenant-acme heavy write workload causing cgroup blkio throttle on shared NVMe; mitigation: live-migrate to dedicated capacity. Action items assigned in the ticket.

Jordan: thanks everyone. good job on fast mitigation. :thumbsup:

Maya: closing out here while Ryan monitors. ping me if it resurfaces.

(End of thread)
